carousels.title: 3 Fragrances That Make People Whisper "What Is That"

slides.name: No. 1
slides.copy: Rare ingredients, no budget cap — once called the world's most expensive perfume for a reason.

slides.name: Eau de New York
slides.copy: Citrus and green tea with a soft musk base — understated enough to make people lean in and ask.

slides.name: Molecule 01
slides.copy: A single molecule, no recognizable notes — it smells like skin, only better, and everyone wants to know why.

carousels.title: 3 Fragrances That Feel Like Old Money

slides.name: Cristalle
slides.copy: Lemon and oakmoss since 1974 — the kind of quiet confidence that doesn't age.

slides.name: Aramis
slides.copy: Leather, moss, and spice from 1963 — often called 'No. 5 for men,' still unmatched.

slides.name: Must de Cartier
slides.copy: Galbanum and jasmine wrapped in vanilla — a scent with a crest, not a logo.

carousels.title: 3 Fragrances That Make a First Date Go Better Than Expected

slides.name: Le Beau
slides.copy: Bergamot and coconut over tonka bean — warm, easy, never overdone.

slides.name: Chloé
slides.copy: Peony and rose with soft amber — the kind of scent that gets remembered past the first course.

slides.name: Romance
slides.copy: Rose and violet leaves with a green edge — the fragrance version of good chemistry.
